data: DL.CODE is not supported on Windows Embedded (commonly used in industrial PCs/PLCs).

CPU requirement: >= 2.0 GHz, RAM requirement: >= 1 GB, OS requirement: Windows 8 or Windows 10 (32/64-bit), Disk requirement: 2 GB (64-bit) or 1 GB (32-bit) free, Network requirement: 100Base-T Ethernet, Display requirement: 19 inch or larger, optimized for 1280×1024.
During long configuration sessions, periodically save to device (Save on Device) to avoid losing changes in temporary memory.
Default configuration is always present, immutable and cannot be deleted.
Permanent memory can store at least 50 configurations when scripts are small (< 2048 chars). Actual capacity varies by configuration and model.
After saving a working setup, perform a Backup to File and/or to an external storage device (e.g., BM100).
To begin Automatic Setup configuration, the reader must be correctly mounted so that its Field of View covers the application reading area.

Procedure: Run Automatic Setup. 1. From Task Area → Open Device Configuration; 2. Select a saved job (Default on new devices); 3. Place target code at correct reading distance; 4. (Optional) Pause image acquisition; 5. Click Focus and wait for completion indication (green line); 6. Click Start Automatic Setup -> device auto-tunes camera and decoding; 7. At the end of the procedure the Automatic Setup Completed! message appears is the processing is success or Code not found if it get error/failed.
During Automatic Setup phases may include initial photometric tuning, code search, search optimization, and end-of-search; not all phases always appear.
Remedy: Repeat Automatic Setup ensuring proper lighting and positioning..
Static vs Dynamic Tuning: Dynamic is required for moving codes to avoid motion blur; set Max Line Speed and Code Resolution when Dynamic is used..

Matrix 220 3xx-x10 includes option: Standard.
Matrix 220 3xx-x10 includes option: DPM.
Matrix 220 3xx-x10 includes option: Static/Dynamic.
Matrix 220 3xx-x10 includes option: Manual Focus.

Matrix 220 3xx-x10 includes option: Polarized/Non-Polarized illumination (US/JP label).
Matrix 220 3xx-040 / 3xx-01A / 3xx-01U options: Static/Dynamic, 1D Codes, 2D Codes, Include Image Filtering.
Matrix 220 3xx-040 / 3xx-01A / 3xx-01U includes option: Static/Dynamic.
Matrix 220 3xx-040 / 3xx-01A / 3xx-01U includes option: 1D Codes.

Use Manual Setup when multiple symbologies, varied image settings, or specific decoding parameters are required.
Procedure: Manual Setup Workflow.
Click Manual Setup; start (Play) then position a Grade A Barcode Test Chart; Pause acquisition.
In Image Settings, click Image Auto-Setup to optimize exposure and gain; choose Static or Dynamic; Apply.
For multiple conditions, add up to 10 Image Settings profiles.
Place application-specific code; re-run Image Auto-Setup to capture lighting/contrast changes.
Enable needed symbologies in Code Settings; remove unused symbologies.
If unknown symbology, use Code Autolearn.
Adjust per-symbology parameters (e.g., Decoding Complexity, Damaged Code Decoding, size, mirroring, gray-level calibration).
Resize/move the code localization box to limit the search area as needed.
Image Settings Profiles: Define up to 10 profiles to handle different, controlled conditions (e.g., lighting). Available in all operating modes..
Automatic Image Settings Selection: Cycles through profiles one per acquisition until a Good Read occurs; throughput may decrease since not every acquisition matches conditions..
When items are grouped by condition, set Start Acquisition From = Last Successful to improve read rate.
External Image Settings Selection: Create Acquisition Sequences; each sequence can be activated by a single external event (string via comms or a digital input)..
Group multiple Image Settings within one Sequence; delete unused sequences; for multi-setting sequences, Start Acquisition From improves rate.
Reduces processing area to where codes exist to increase frame rate and performance (Matrix 220 frame rate depends on window size).
Click Add Cropping Region; a blue border (initially full FoV) appears.
Resize by dragging edges (pixel indices shown); move by dragging the center.
Alternatively set exact size/position via Cropping Region Area (Width, Height, Left, Top).
Decoding Complexity (Data Matrix) options: Low, Medium, High, Very High.
Decoding Complexity (Data Matrix) option available: Low.
Decoding Complexity (Data Matrix) option available: Medium.
Decoding Complexity (Data Matrix) option available: High.
Decoding Complexity (Data Matrix) option available: Very High.
Use the lowest value that guarantees good decoding to minimize time; Very High improves decode rate on low-quality/small codes but may be slower.
Decoding Method (QR) options: Dot Peen Decoding.
Decoding Method (QR) option available: Dot Peen Decoding.
Improves decode rate for low-quality DPM QR codes with dot-peened modules.
Illumination guidelines: Recommended Illumination (summary).
Printed labels/opaque flat surfaces: White, non-polarized or polarized, or diffused lighting are suitable.
Rough surfaces: External diffused lighting (e.g., ring light) often preferred.
Flat surfaces with machining marks: Polarized or diffused to reduce glare.
Highly reflective flat surfaces: Polarized/diffused lighting to mitigate glare.
Curved surfaces: Choose lighting that minimizes specular reflections across curvature.
Illumination legend: 'OK' means Suggested, 'Compatible' means Usable, 'X' means Not recommended.
Select DPM model with Blue or Red illuminator to maximize code/background contrast.
Lighting color similar to code makes code appear brighter; opposite color makes it darker (chromatic circle principle).
White light (STD) gives good contrast on mixed colors; for red or blue-coded items, match illuminator to optimize contrast accordingly.
Topic: Image Filters (pre-processing).
Image filter 'Erode': Expands dark zones to improve readability on certain marks..
Image filter 'Dilate': Expands white zones to improve readability..
Image filter 'Close': Fills dark defects in white regions..
Image filter 'Open': Removes white defects in dark regions..
Image filter 'Contrast Stretching': Maximizes overall image contrast..
Image filter 'Histogram Equalization': Uniforms gray level distribution..
Image filter 'Smoothing': Suppresses small, insignificant details (noise)..
Image filter 'Sharpening': Improves slightly out-of-focus images..
Image filter 'Deblurring': Reduces motion/defocus blur..
Image filter 'Black Enhancement': Nonlinear increase of black level for light images..
Image filter 'White Enhancement': Nonlinear increase of white level for dark images..
Image filter 'Contrast Enhancement': Boosts contrast without over-amplifying noise in uniform regions..
DL.CODE supports connecting to Matrix 220 via onboard Ethernet.
For lengthy configurations, periodically save to device to avoid losing temporary changes.
The Default configuration is immutable and cannot be deleted.
After saving configuration, perform Backup to File and/or external device such as BM100.
Automatic Setup begins by acquiring images from the device.
Focusing should be completed before Automatic Setup.
Not all Automatic Setup phases are always displayed.
Use Test Mode to verify correct operation after Automatic Setup.
If Automatic Setup cannot find the code, check lighting and object positioning and retry.
Dynamic tuning is required for moving codes to reduce motion blur.
When Dynamic tuning is selected, configure Max Line Speed and Code Resolution.
Manual Setup is recommended when multiple symbologies or different image settings are needed.
Up to 10 different Image Settings can be configured in Manual Setup.
Re-run Image Auto-Setup when switching to an application-specific code to capture lighting or contrast differences.
Use Code Autolearn if the code symbology is unknown.
Resize or move the code localization box to limit the search area to speed up decoding.
Multi Image Acquisition enables a database of parameter groups for different controlled conditions.
Multi Image Acquisition works in all Operating Modes.
Automatic Image Settings Selection cycles through profiles one per acquisition until a Good Read occurs.
Throughput may be lower with Automatic Image Settings Selection because not all acquisitions match the condition.
Set 'Start Acquisition From' to 'Last Successful' to improve read rate for grouped items with the same condition.
External Image Settings Selection uses Acquisition Sequences activated by a single event (communication string or digital input).
Multiple Image Settings can be grouped within a single Acquisition Sequence.
'Start Acquisition From' improves read rate for sequences with more than one Image Setting.
Image cropping reduces the processing window to areas where codes are present.
On Matrix 220, frame rate depends on the number of rows and columns in the defined window.
Add Cropping Region creates a blue border equal to the full field of view by default.
Cropping region can be resized by dragging edges and moved by dragging the center.
Cropping region size and position can be set numerically via Width, Height, Left, and Top.
For Data Matrix, higher Decoding Complexity improves decode rate on poor-quality or small codes but can increase decoding time.
For QR codes, the Dot Peen Decoding method improves reading of low-quality DPM marks with dot-peened modules.
Choose DPM model illuminator color (Red or Blue) to maximize contrast between code and background.
Illuminating with the same color as the code makes the code appear brighter.
Illuminating with the opposite color makes the code appear darker.
White light provides good contrast for mixed color codes and backgrounds.
Avoid glare from internal illuminators overlapping the code in the field of view.
If glare covers the code at the FoV center, try placing the code at top, bottom, left, or right of the FoV.
Non-polarized and diffused illuminators can provide good reads where polarized light does not due to contrast limits.
The Erode filter enlarges dark regions to aid readability.
The Dilate filter enlarges white regions to aid readability.
The Close filter fills dark defects in white areas.
The Open filter removes white defects in dark areas.
Contrast Stretching maximizes image contrast.
Histogram Equalization makes gray-level distribution more uniform.
Smoothing reduces small, insignificant details.
Sharpening improves slightly out-of-focus images.
Deblurring reduces blur from motion or defocus.
Black Enhancement increases black levels in light images nonlinearly.
White Enhancement increases white levels in dark images nonlinearly.
Contrast Enhancement boosts contrast without over-amplifying noise in uniform regions.
PWR LED: Blue, indicates the reader is powered.
NET LED: Yellow, indicates connection to the on-board Ethernet network.
STATUS LED: Red, indicates NO READ result in normal operation.
COM LED: Yellow, indicates active communication on the main serial port. When connected through CBX500 to Fieldbus, it remains active due to polling even if no data is transmitted.
TRIGGER LED: Yellow, indicates the reading phase status.
GOOD LED: Green, confirms successful reading.
READY LED: Green, indicates the reader is ready to operate.
Startup: During reset or restart, the five LEDs blink for one second.
X-PRESS Mode: In X-PRESS Configuration mode, LED colors and meanings differ as defined in the X-PRESS HMI.
Keypad Button: By default, pressing the button starts the X-PRESS interface for quick installation without a PC.
Product Label Example: Voltage 10–30 VDC, Current 0.40–0.14 A, Model MATRIX 220 382-010, Serial COOP20345, Date September 2020, MAC 00:07:BE:00:7C:44.
Aiming System: Two red LED pointers project equidistant squares; the code should be centered between them.
LED Spots: Two LEDs (green/red) illuminate the target area to signal events (Good Read/No Read), configurable in DL.CODE.
ID-NET: Built-in high-speed interface for interconnecting readers.
ID-NET Synchronized: Multiple readers read different sides of the same object, sharing one sensor, sending one combined message.
ID-NET Multidata: Multiple independent readers on separate conveyors, each sends its own data to the host.
X-PRESS HMI: Intuitive interface with 5 LEDs and one push button.
X-PRESS Functions: Test (bar graph), Aim/Autofocus (LED pointers), Setup (Exposure/Gain calibration), Learn (auto-detect and configure codes).
Test Mode: LEDs show Good Read Rate thresholds (≥20%, ≥40%, ≥60%, ≥75%, ≥95%). In NO READ, only the red LED blinks. Exit by pressing the button or after 3 minutes (auto-timeout).
Focus/Aim Mode: LED pointers turn on and blink, aiding code alignment. Exit by pressing the button or after short delay.
Setup Mode: Calibrates image parameters. Success: parameters saved, 3 high beeps. Failure: after ~5s, exit without saving, long low beep.
Learn Mode: Auto-detects a code. Success: parameters saved, Green Spot activates, 3 high beeps. Failure: after ~3 minutes, exit without saving, long low beep.
Error Indication: STATUS (red) and READY (green) LEDs blink simultaneously. Detailed errors can be enabled in DL.CODE Monitor.
Illumination Standard: 4 white LEDs.
Illumination High Power: 8 white LEDs, double power.
Illumination DPM: Top/Bottom Diffused and Polarized/Non-Polarized, Red/Blue options.
Illumination High Power DPM Red: Double power for Polarized and Non-Polarized.

Illumination Combinations: Standard White (Top+Bottom, Top, Bottom), DPM Red/Blue (Diffused Top+Bottom, Diffused Top, Diffused Bottom, Non-Polarized, Polarized), High Power White/Red (Central+Top/Bottom Chain, Central Chain, Top/Bottom Chain), High Power DPM Red (Polarized, Non-Polarized).

Reading Capabilities: Omnidirectional reading for documents and mail, damaged/overprinted/reflected/curved codes, DPM on metal/PCB, improved contrast with Red/Blue illumination, YAG filter models for real-time laser codes.
Digimarc Support: Models 937900017 and 937900018.
HDR: Enhances low-intensity pixels, improves contrast, allows shorter exposure and higher line speed. Recommended Gain Multiplier = x1.
UV Model: Matrix 220 3U2-01U 1.2MP STD-UV 7MM HP.
UV Illumination: 365 nm excitation, with 415 nm Long Pass filter. Requires inks sensitive to 365 nm.
UV Gain: Higher gain often needed due to weak fluorescence signal, especially in dynamic applications with Very High Power lighting.
UV Lighting Modes: High Power-Strobed for static/semi-static, Very High Power for dynamic.
UV Note: Standard reading diagrams don’t apply; performance depends on ink/surface and must be tested.
Package Contents: Reader (with connector plug/cover), Quick Reference Guide, Test Chart, Mounting Kit (2 screws, 2 washers, 1 bracket).
IP Protection Ethernet Models: IP67 protection with sealing plug when Ethernet unused.
IP Protection PoE Models: COM/Trigger connector cover provides protection when unused.

Problem: DL.CODE Installation Autorun or Start.hta doesn’t; Suggestion: Check Windows settings to see if Autorun is disabled. Associate the file type .hta with the Microsoft HTML Applicationhost mshta.exe in Windows\System32.

Problem: The “POWER” LED is not lit; Suggestion: Is power connected? If using a power adapter (like PG6000), is it connected to wall outlet? If using rail power, does rail have power? If using CBX, does it have power (check switch and LED)?Check if you are referring to the M12 17-pin connector or to the CBX spring clamp connectors. Measure Voltage either at pin 1 and pin 2 (for 17-pin connector)or at spring clamp Vdc and GND (for CBX).

Problem: the ”TRIGGER” LED is not blinking while the External Trigger is switching; Suggestion: Check if you are referring to the 17-pin connector or to the CBX spring clamp connectors; Is the sensor connected to Input 1 or Input 2?Is power supplied to the photo sensor?For NPN configuration, is power supplied to one of the two I1 or I2 signals (A or B)? For PNP configuration, is one of the two I1 or I2 signals grounded (A or B)? Are the photo sensor LEDS (if any) working correctly? Is the sensor/reflector system aligned (if present)? On the Reading Phase step check the Input 1 or Input 2 Debouncing Time parameter setting. On the Reading Phase step check the settings for AcquisitionTrigger, Reading Phase-ON, and Reading Phase-OFF parameters.

Problem: the ”TRIGGER” LED is not blinking when using serial trigger source; Suggestion: On the Reading Phase step check the settings for Acquisition Trigger, Reading Phase-ON, and Reading Phase-OFF parameters. Are the COM port parameters (Baud Rate, Parity, Data Bits, Stop Bits) correctly assigned? On the Reading Phase step check the settings of Acquisition Trigger String, Reading Phase-ON String, and Reading Phase- OFF String parameters. Is the serial trigger source correctly connected?
Problem: the ”TRIGGER” LED is correctly blinking but no image is displayed in the DL.CODE window; Suggestion: Is the Phase frequency lower than the maximum frame rate?
Problem: the ”TRIGGER” LED is not blinking in Continuous Mode. Verify the correct software configuration settings.

Problem: the ”TRIGGER” LED is correctly blinking but no result is transmitted by the reader at the end of the reading phase collection. Suggestion: Check the Code Collection parameters on the Reading Phase step and the Data Formatting parameters on the Data Formatting step.
Problem: Image not clear; Suggestion: verify the Focus procedure;
Problem: Image focused but not decoded; Suggestion: verify the Calibrate Image Density procedure

Problem: the reader always transmits the No Read Message; Suggestion: check Position the reader; Tune the Acquisition Delay on Trigger, if the moving code is out of the reader field of view; Set the Continuous Operating Mode if no external trigger source is available; Tune the Image Settings to improve the code image quality; Check the parameter settings in the Advanced Setup step: 2D Codes, 1D Codes, and Postal Codes; View the full resolution code image to check the printing or marking quality.

Problem: reader is not transmitting anything to the host; Suggestion: Is the serial cable wiring correct? If using CBX, be sure the RS422 termination switch is OFF. Are the host serial port settings the same as the reader serial port settings? In DL.CODE Device menu > Settings > Settings > LED Configuration, the COM LED Function can be configured to indicate Main Serial Port TX or Main Serial Port RX.

Problem: data transferred to the host are incorrect, corrupted or incomplete. Suggestion: Are the host serial port settings the same as the reader serial port settings? In the DL.CODE Data Formatting step check the settings of Header and Terminator String parameters. In the DL.CODE Data Formatting step, check the various Message Field parameter settings.

Problem: cannot access environment parameters in DL.CODE (Device>Settings>Settings menu item is grey); Suggestion: Are you using the Installer - Expert User level? If not change it in the Options>Change User menu.

Problem: How do I obtain my reader Serial Number? Suggestion: The reader Serial Number consists of 9 characters: one letter, 2 numbers, another letter followed by 5 numbers. The reader Serial Number is printed on a label that is affixed to the case or connector block of the reader. The Serial Number is also visible from the DL.CODE Device List Area.
